root_cause.text: F2FS was creating per-superblock xattr slab caches with device-specific names (e.g., "f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3"), causing multiple filesystems with identical xattr sizes to share the same underlying kmem_cache structure while maintaining separate cache references, leading to incomplete cache destruction and name collision warnings on remount.
root_cause.evidence: The patch description explicitly states: "if we created two slab caches, named f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3 and f2fs_xattr_entry-7:7, and they have the same slab size. Actually, slab system will only create one slab cache core structure which has slab name of 'f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3', and two slab caches share the same structure and cache address. So, if we destroy f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3 cache w/ cache address, it will decrease reference count of slab cache, rather than release slab cache entirely, since there is one more user has referenced the cache." The fix removes per-sb slab cache creation (`sbi->inline_xattr_slab` and related fields removed from f2fs_sb_info struct) and replaces it with a single global `inline_xattr_slab` initialized at module load time with a fixed name "f2fs_xattr_entry" and constant size `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE`, eliminating the device-specific naming collision issue.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove inline xattr slab cache fields from f2fs_sb_info structure, likely consolidating or eliminating inline xattr slab management.
intent_record.what: Removed three lines from struct f2fs_sb_info: a comment line and two struct members (inline_xattr_slab pointer and inline_xattr_slab_size unsigned int) along with their associated comment.
intent_record.how: This removal eliminates the inline xattr slab cache management fields from the f2fs superblock info structure. Any code that previously accessed these members through the f2fs_sb_info structure will no longer be able to do so, requiring either deletion of dependent code or refactoring to use an alternative mechanism for inline xattr slab management.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant xattr cache destruction call that is now handled elsewhere in the shutdown sequence or was causing incorrect cleanup ordering.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi) from the f2fs_put_super function, which was previously located after f2fs_destroy_page_array_cache(sbi) and before the CONFIG_QUOTA conditional block.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the cleanup/destruction of xattr caches during filesystem unmount. The xattr caches will no longer be explicitly freed at this point in the shutdown sequence, potentially causing them to be cleaned up elsewhere or at a different time in the shutdown process.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove xattr cache initialization and fix error handling to prevent cleanup of unallocated resources.
intent_record.what: Removed the f2fs_init_xattr_caches() function call and its error handling block (4 lines), and changed the error goto label in f2fs_init_page_array_cache() from 'free_xattr_cache' to 'free_percpu'.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the initialization of xattr caches during f2fs superblock setup. If f2fs_init_page_array_cache() fails, the cleanup path now jumps directly to free_percpu instead of attempting to free xattr caches that were never allocated. This prevents potential use-after-free or double-free issues in the error handling path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant xattr cache cleanup from error path, likely because xattr cache destruction is now handled elsewhere or the cleanup order was corrected.
intent_record.what: Removed two lines from the error handling path in f2fs_fill_super(): the label 'free_xattr_cache:' and the call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches(sbi).
intent_record.how: This eliminates a cleanup step during filesystem initialization failure. If initialization fails after xattr caches are created, they will no longer be explicitly destroyed at this point in the error unwinding sequence, potentially leaving xattr cache resources unreleased.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize xattr cache before filesystem registration and add proper error handling to prevent resource leaks if filesystem registration fails after xattr cache is allocated.
intent_record.what: Reordered initialization sequence to call f2fs_init_xattr_cache() before register_filesystem(), added corresponding error handling path with f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache() cleanup label, and inserted new error goto target free_xattr_cache between the xattr cache initialization check and the filesystem registration.
intent_record.how: This change ensures the xattr cache is initialized before the filesystem is registered with the kernel. If xattr cache initialization fails, it jumps to free_xattr_cache label. If filesystem registration subsequently fails, it now jumps to free_xattr_cache (which cleans up xattr cache) before proceeding to free_casefold_cache, establishing proper cleanup ordering in reverse initialization order.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing xattr cache cleanup in F2FS module exit to prevent memory leak.
intent_record.what: Added a call to f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache() in the exit_f2fs_fs() function, positioned before the existing f2fs_destroy_casefold_cache() call.
intent_record.how: This ensures that the xattr cache is properly cleaned up and freed when the F2FS filesystem module is unloaded. Without this call, the xattr cache would remain allocated in memory, causing a resource leak during module exit.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor inline xattr slab allocation to use a static module-level cache and constant size instead of per-superblock instances.
intent_record.what: Added a static module-level variable `inline_xattr_slab` and changed two references from `sbi->inline_xattr_slab_size` to `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE` and from `sbi->inline_xattr_slab` to `inline_xattr_slab` in the xattr_alloc function.
intent_record.how: This change moves the inline xattr slab cache from a per-superblock instance (sbi->inline_xattr_slab) to a static module-level singleton (inline_xattr_slab), and replaces a dynamic size comparison with a compile-time constant (DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE). This reduces per-superblock memory overhead and simplifies size checking by using a fixed constant instead of reading from the superblock info structure.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix xattr_free to use the global inline_xattr_slab variable instead of the per-superblock reference, ensuring consistency with the allocation path and correct memory deallocation.
intent_record.what: Changed `kmem_cache_free(sbi->inline_xattr_slab, xattr_addr)` to `kmem_cache_free(inline_xattr_slab, xattr_addr)` in the xattr_free function, replacing a per-superblock reference with a static global variable reference.
intent_record.how: This change makes the inline xattr slab deallocation use a static global `inline_xattr_slab` instead of accessing it through the superblock info structure `sbi->inline_xattr_slab`. This eliminates an indirection through the sbi pointer and directly references the module-level cache, which is consistent with the allocation path that also uses the global static variable.

intent_record.intent_summary: Convert xattr cache from per-superblock to global singleton model with simplified initialization and fixed slab size.
intent_record.what: Refactored xattr cache initialization from per-superblock to global: renamed f2fs_init_xattr_caches to f2fs_init_xattr_cache with __init annotation, removed sbi parameter and device-specific slab naming logic, replaced dynamic slab_size calculation with DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE constant, changed inline_xattr_slab from per-sbi to global variable, simplified error handling to ternary expression, and updated corresponding destroy function to operate on global cache.
intent_record.how: This change converts xattr cache management from a per-filesystem-instance model (one cache per mounted f2fs) to a single global cache shared across all f2fs instances. The __init annotation marks the function for kernel module initialization. Device-specific naming is removed since there's now only one global cache. The slab size becomes fixed (DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE) rather than dynamically calculated per superblock. Runtime behavior changes: all f2fs instances now share the same memory cache pool instead of maintaining separate caches.

intent_record.intent_summary: Define a new macro constant for default xattr slab size to centralize and standardize xattr memory allocation calculations.
intent_record.what: Added a new macro definition `DEFAULT_XATTR_SLAB_SIZE` that calculates the default extended attribute slab size by multiplying `DEFAULT_INLINE_XATTR_ADDRS` by the size of `__le32` and adding `XATTR_PADDING_SIZE`.
intent_record.how: This macro provides a centralized constant for the default xattr slab allocation size, enabling consistent memory allocation calculations throughout the codebase. It derives its value from existing related macros, ensuring the slab size accounts for both the address array and required padding.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor xattr cache management from per-superblock to module-level initialization by renaming functions, adding __init modifier, and removing sb_info parameters.
intent_record.what: Changed two function declarations: (1) renamed f2fs_init_xattr_caches to f2fs_init_xattr_cache and added __init modifier, changed parameter from 'struct f2fs_sb_info *' to 'void'; (2) renamed f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches to f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache and removed parameter 'struct f2fs_sb_info *', changing it to 'void'.
intent_record.how: These changes convert xattr cache initialization/destruction from per-superblock operations into module-level initialization/cleanup routines. The __init modifier marks f2fs_init_xattr_cache as initialization-only code that can be freed after boot. Removing the sb_info parameter indicates the cache is now globally managed rather than per-filesystem instance, affecting how xattr caches are allocated and deallocated at module load/unload time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Refactor xattr cache stub functions to remove sbi parameter dependency, add __init annotation for boot-time initialization, and rename to reflect singular cache management.
intent_record.what: Two static inline function declarations were modified: (1) f2fs_init_xattr_caches renamed to f2fs_init_xattr_cache with __init annotation added and parameter changed from 'struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi' to 'void'; (2) f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches renamed to f2fs_destroy_xattr_cache with parameter changed from 'struct f2fs_sb_info *sbi' to 'void'.
intent_record.how: These are stub implementations used when xattr support is disabled (CONFIG_F2FS_XATTR not set). The changes remove the sbi parameter dependency, making these functions no longer require filesystem superblock information. The __init annotation on the init function indicates it will be discarded after kernel boot, reducing memory footprint. The renamed functions (singular 'cache' instead of plural 'caches') suggest a shift from managing multiple caches to a single cache structure.

consistency_review.core_intent: Refactor xattr cache management from per-superblock to global module-level singleton model with boot-time initialization.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by converting xattr cache management from per-superblock (device-specific) to global module-level singleton model. This eliminates the creation of multiple device-specific named caches (e.g., 'f2fs_xattr_entry-7:3'), preventing cache sharing issues, name collisions, and incomplete destruction that occurred when multiple filesystems with identical xattr sizes reused the same underlying kmem_cache structure.

This group removes redundant cleanup operations that are already handled elsewhere. The vulnerability root cause is about improper cache creation with device-specific names causing sharing and collision issues. Removing duplicate cleanup doesn't address the core problem of how caches are created, named, or shared across multiple filesystems. The fix would need to address cache creation/naming logic, not just cleanup redundancy.

This group directly addresses the vulnerability by removing xattr cache initialization, which eliminates the root cause of per-superblock xattr slab caches being created with device-specific names. By preventing cache initialization, it avoids the name collision and incomplete cache destruction issues that occurred when multiple filesystems shared the same underlying kmem_cache structure.

The group addresses resource leak prevention and initialization ordering, but does not address the core vulnerability: the device-specific naming scheme that causes cache sharing and collision warnings. The root cause requires eliminating device names from cache identifiers or implementing proper per-filesystem cache isolation, neither of which this group accomplishes.

The group addresses a memory leak by adding xattr cache cleanup during module exit, which is a general resource management fix. However, the vulnerability root cause is specifically about per-superblock cache creation with device-specific names causing cache sharing conflicts and name collisions on remount. This group does not address the core issue of improper cache naming scheme or the mechanism that causes multiple filesystems to share the same underlying kmem_cache structure.

This group directly addresses a core aspect of the vulnerability root cause. The vulnerability involves inconsistency between xattr allocation and deallocation paths due to per-superblock cache references. By fixing xattr_free to use the global inline_xattr_slab variable instead of per-superblock references, this change ensures consistent memory deallocation and eliminates the mismatch that caused incomplete cache destruction and name collisions. This is a direct fix to the root cause mechanism.

This group only defines a macro constant for xattr slab size standardization. The vulnerability root cause is about per-superblock slab cache creation with device-specific names causing cache sharing and name collision issues. Defining a size constant does not address the core problem of how slab caches are created, named, or managed across multiple filesystems. This is a refactoring/standardization change, not a fix for the cache naming or lifecycle management issues.

Per-superblock allocation of xattr slab caches with device-specific names causes multiple filesystems to share the same underlying kmem_cache while maintaining separate references, preventing proper cleanup.
Uses per-superblock slab size comparison that depends on the per-superblock cache allocation model, which is the root cause of the vulnerability.
Calls per-superblock xattr cache initialization during mount, creating device-specific named caches that collide and cause incomplete destruction on remount.

vuln_statements.explanation: Creates device-specific slab cache names that cause name collisions when multiple filesystems have identical xattr sizes. This is the primary vulnerability - the device-specific naming scheme (major:minor) causes multiple superblocks to attempt creating caches with the same name, leading to shared kmem_cache structures with separate references and incomplete destruction on unmount.

Per-superblock allocation of xattr slab caches using device-specific names causes multiple filesystems to share the same underlying kmem_cache while maintaining separate per-superblock references (sbi->inline_xattr_slab), preventing proper cleanup and causing cache destruction warnings.
Calls per-superblock xattr cache initialization during mount, which creates device-specific named caches that collide across multiple filesystem instances and cause incomplete destruction on remount.
Uses per-superblock slab size comparison that depends on the vulnerable per-superblock cache allocation model, maintaining the dependency on device-specific cache instances.

Frees from per-superblock slab cache reference that may not match the actual kmem_cache used for allocation when multiple filesystems share the same underlying cache due to name collisions, causing use-after-free or double-free conditions.

Author: Chao Yu <chao@kernel.org>
Date:   Tue Feb 25 18:17:10 2020 +0800

    f2fs: use kmem_cache pool during inline xattr lookups
    
    It's been observed that kzalloc() on lookup_all_xattrs() are called millions
    of times on Android, quickly becoming the top abuser of slub memory allocator.
    
    Use a dedicated kmem cache pool for xattr lookups to mitigate this.
    
    Signed-off-by: Park Ju Hyung <qkrwngud825@gmail.com>
    Signed-o
bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the vulnerable construct in the new `f2fs_init_xattr_caches()` function. Specifically, line `sprintf(slab_name, "f2fs_xattr_entry-%u:%u", MAJOR(dev), MINOR(dev))` creates per-superblock xattr slab caches with device-specific names. This causes the root cause vulnerability: multiple filesystems with identical xattr sizes will share the same underlying kmem_cache structure (because they have the same device major:minor) while maintaining separate cache references in different sbi structures. The function then calls `f2fs_kmem_cache_create(slab_name, ...)` which will either reuse an existing cache with that name or create a new one, but the corresponding `f2fs_destroy_xattr_caches()` will always attempt to destroy it, leading to incomplete cache destruction and name collision warnings on remount. The fix is not present - the code lacks proper reference counting or a global cache pool to handle multiple filesystems with the same device and xattr size.
